Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

islasso 1.7.0

Numerical core

  • The Fortran routines have been replaced by a new core written in C on top of the BLAS/LAPACK libraries of R (no Fortran compiler is needed any more to install from source).
  • At fixed standard errors the smoothed estimating equation is the gradient of a smooth convex objective; it is now solved by undamped majorise-minimise iterations (default, the same fixed point as before with about half of the factorisations) or by Newton’s method with line search (is.control(inner = "newton")).
  • Only the diagonal of the sandwich matrix and the pseudo hat values are computed during the iterations (about 4 times fewer flops per iteration); the full covariance matrix is computed once, at convergence.
  • New Woodbury back end used when the number of columns exceeds twice the number of observations: cost O(n^2 p) instead of O(p^3) per step (is.control(solver = )).
  • islasso.path() fits every model as islasso() would at the same lambda (glmnet starting values, standard errors started at their default values), so that path and single fits agree (in 1.6.x the standard errors were carried over along the path and the effective degrees of freedom, hence the information criteria, depended on the path); the models can be fitted in parallel with is.control(ncores = ) (socket cluster); computes X’X once for the Gaussian family, keeps all the models (with a convergence flag, column conv of Info) and no longer drops covariates permanently from the path.
  • For the Gaussian family the whole induced-smoothing iteration runs in compiled code.
  • islasso.path() stores the standardized scores (Score), and plot.islasso.path() gains yvar = "score", the induced-smoothing analogue of the lasso optimality conditions; all the profiles (including the gradient) are drawn against log(lambda).
  • No more large arrays on the stack (possible crashes with large n * p in 1.6.x).

Models

  • Any family object accepted by glm() can be used (all the links of binomial, poisson, Gamma; inverse.gaussian; quasi families; MASS::negative.binomial(), …): the IRLS loop is driven by the family object, with step halving when the linear predictor becomes invalid.
  • With stand = TRUE the penalty now acts on the standardised coefficients, as in glmnet (whose cross-validation provides lambda when it is missing): before, the estimator penalised the coefficients on the original scale while glmnet worked on the standardised ones. Results change for covariates that are not standardised.
  • The scale of lambda is sum(weights) times the glmnet scale (equal to n with unit weights).
  • is.control(seed = ) is now used (reproducible cross-validation; the RNG state is restored).

Bug fixes

  • Models without intercept and stand = TRUE were centred, changing the model.
  • The probit inverse link had a wrong clamping threshold (8.1e6 instead of 8.13), producing infinite weights for large linear predictors.
  • aic.islasso() refitted the model with the IRLS working weights as prior weights; it now optimises over log(lambda).
  • AICc had an extra factor n; GCV is now n * deviance / (n - df)^2.
  • islasso.path(): rows of fitted values/residuals could be misaligned with the coefficients when some fit failed.
  • relax.islasso() failed for models without intercept and used an infinite lambda.
  • predict(type = "coefficients", se.fit = TRUE) failed; summary.islasso.path() printed the log-likelihood as residual deviance; path methods returned NA at the largest lambda.
  • An offset given as a covariate name removed that covariate from the model.
  • logLik() is NA for families without likelihood (quasi).
  • anova(): the overall Wald test uses a generalised inverse, so it no longer fails when the covariance matrix of the hypotheses is numerically singular (degrees of freedom = its rank).
  • The dispersion is protected against non-positive residual degrees of freedom for all families.

Other changes

  • Influence measures and diagnostic plots use the leverages of the sandwich Hessian (no QR of the augmented design, no n x n hat matrix).
  • glmnet moved from Depends to Imports; the startup banner and the dependencies on cli and gridExtra have been removed.
  • New vignettes: methodology and algorithm, GLMs and families, high-dimensional data.
  • Unit tests (testthat).

islasso 1.6.2 (2025-11-15)

CRAN release: 2025-11-15

  • Fixed the number of arguments in a call to the internal routine inv_posdef.

islasso 1.6.1 (2025-08-17)

CRAN release: 2025-11-14

  • Created GitHub page and website.
  • Created introductory vignette.
  • Fortran routines updated and speeded up (~2x).
  • Manuals updated.
  • Added new function relax.islasso(), which allows fitting a relaxed islasso model by selecting variables to remain unpenalized. Variables can be specified either by name or by index, or automatically selected according to a significance level (alpha). This extension provides additional flexibility in post-selection inference.
  • Some bugs fixed.

islasso 1.6.0 (2025-07-30)

CRAN release: 2025-07-31

Performance & Refactoring

  • Core computational routines have been cleaned up, and some bugs have been fixed.
  • Legacy R routines have been revised, cleaned, and commented. Minor inconsistencies have been addressed.

Documentation

  • Help files and function manuals are now fully managed via roxygen2, with substantial updates to usage examples and descriptions.

Visualization

  • All plotting functions have been refactored to use the ggplot2 framework for consistent and modern graphics.

User Experience

  • A custom ASCII startup banner has been added on package attach, providing a welcoming and informative message.

islasso 1.4.0

CRAN release: 2021-10-15

  • New optimization algorithm for the ‘islasso’ method. The algorithm is now stable for all the implemented distributions.
  • In aic.islasso() function the available methods are “AIC”, “BIC”, “AICc”, “eBIC”, “GCV”, “GIC”.
  • New class of functions named islasso.path created. The main function islasso.path() builds the coefficient profile for a fixed sequence of lambda values.
  • New function GoF.islasso.path() extracts the optimal tuning parameter minimizing a fixed criterion. Available criteria are the same as in aic.islasso().
  • Some bugs fixed.

islasso 1.2.1

islasso 1.2.0

CRAN release: 2021-01-21

  • New implementation of the estimating algorithm. Now islasso is much stabler and faster.
  • New function: general linear hypotheses for linear combinations of the regression coefficients, including confidence intervals.
  • Prediction function includes confidence intervals for the fitted values.
  • Step halving with Armijo’s rule improved.
  • Convergence criterion improved.
  • Some bugs fixed.

islasso 1.1.0

CRAN release: 2019-06-25

  • New implementation of the estimating algorithm. Now islasso is much stabler and faster, reducing the number of iterations to reach convergence.
  • Step halving with Armijo’s rule implemented.
  • Elastic-net approach added via alpha parameter in the objective function (as in glmnet).
  • Summary method now includes degrees of freedom for each covariate, with choice between t-test or z-test (only for Gaussian family).
  • optim.islasso renamed to aic.islasso; interval specification no longer required.
  • islasso.control renamed to is.control; control parameters modified.
  • Two trace versions implemented in is.control: compact (trace = 1) and verbose (trace = 2).
  • Some bugs fixed.
